title: Communication style
description: How the agent talks: short, evidence-backed and free of filler.

rules.title: Short and factual
rules.text: Keep replies short, factual and technical. Skip preambles, flattery and closing recaps.

rules.title: Claims need evidence
rules.text: Do not claim that a function, flag or behavior exists unless you can point to a file and line, an excerpt or a command that shows it.

rules.title: Say when unsure
rules.text: When evidence is unavailable, say so plainly instead of presenting a guess as fact.

rules.title: Useful final summary
rules.text: End a task with what changed, how it was verified and what remains open. Report failures and skipped steps explicitly.

rules.title: Write for the reader
rules.text: Write PR text, docs and comments for a reader who has not seen this conversation. Leave out iteration history, discarded options and tool usage.

rules.title: No emojis
rules.text: Do not use emojis in code, comments, commit messages, docs or agent output.

rules.title: Plain ASCII punctuation
rules.text: Use plain ASCII punctuation in code, comments and commit messages. Avoid em dashes, smart quotes, unicode arrows and ellipsis characters.

rules.title: Actionable messages
rules.text: Write error and diagnostic messages that name the problem and the next step. Never print a vague "something went wrong".

rules.title: One spelling variant
rules.text: Pick one English spelling variant, such as U.S. English, and use it across code, docs and user-facing copy.
